sentence: This project studies how brainwide neural representations of flavor change when feedback from the gut arrives, shaping aversions for specific tastes.
This project studies how a mutation that raises the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease affects immune cells in the coronary vasculature.
This project uses many kinds of data from people living with HIV to build predictive models that help prevent virologic failure.
This project uses functional neuroimaging and machine learning to study how emotional states change over time in people with bipolar disorder.
This project uses tissue engineering to recreate the functions of the periosteum so that bone allograft can heal and integrate.
This project provides electrophysiological studies of brain slices, using optogenetics and calcium imaging, for other projects.
This project builds a rapid monitoring system that gives immediate information about phenylalanine levels for children with Phenylketonuria.
This project uses airway organoids to find out how airway epithelial cells and macrophages communicate.
This project tests a molecularly targeted agent in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and looks for the sources of drug resistance.
This project studies how a core circadian clock protein controls timing in synapses and sleep and wake behavior.
This project builds a tool that measures lesions on neonatal brain MRI to sort types of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and predict prognosis.
This project compares aging clocks based on DNA methylation, proteomics and MRI to see how they relate to Alzheimer disease progression.
This project develops magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission tomography methods to detect reperfusion injury in the heart.
This project brings together research on cancer risk assessment, early detection and interception, including risk prediction models and molecular markers.
This project studies how mutations in a part of cohesin change 3D genome organization in glioblastoma multiforme cells and tumors.
This project studies how bacteria use random switching, memory and recombination to survive nutrient starvation and antibiotics.
This project studies how HIV passes through the nuclear pore complex and how that choice directs viral genomes to specific nuclear environments.
This project tries to turn basic findings into a therapy that improves corneal transplants and reduces graft failures.
This project studies risk and protective factors from adolescence to adulthood that shape mental health, using genotyping and a prevention trial of low-income families.
This project studies how coronary microvascular dysfunction affects heart function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, using mice.
